title: galaxy_rotation_curves.ipynb

canonical_node.axiom: The chi-field modified gravity must produce galaxy rotation curves consistent with observations without invoking dark matter, using the same coupling constant xi constrained by the Hubble tension test.
definitions: Chi-field: a coherence field that modifies gravity via position-dependent effective gravitational constant G_eff.
G-M symmetry pair: the symmetry structure coupling chi-field to mass-energy.
Rotation curve: the orbital velocity v(r) of stars as a function of radius r from galactic center.
Newtonian prediction: v(r) = sqrt(G M(r) / r), where M(r) is enclosed mass.
Flat rotation curve: observed v(r) approximately constant at large r.
Coupling constant xi: the chi-field coupling parameter, already constrained by Hubble tension test.
derivation: Newtonian gravity predicts v(r) falls as r^(-1/2) at large radii for disk galaxies.
Observations show v(r) is roughly constant, indicating a gravitational anomaly.
In chi-field gravity, G_eff depends on local chi-field value, which depends on matter density via G-M symmetry.
In low-density regions (galactic outskirts), chi-field relaxes to a different value, increasing G_eff.
This position-dependent G_eff produces an effective additional gravitational pull at large radii, flattening the rotation curve.
The notebook fits chi-field parameters to observed rotation curves, using xi already constrained by Hubble tension.
The fits are comparable to dark matter halo models, without additional free parameters.
canonical_node.action: Compute chi-field predictions for galaxy rotation curves and compare to observed data, using xi from Hubble tension constraints, to test consistency without dark matter.
boundary: Does not prove chi-field is the correct explanation for dark matter.
Does not claim superiority over dark matter models; only consistency.
Does not include full observational error bars in fitting.
Does not address all galaxy types or detailed baryonic effects.
test: Fit chi-field model to observed rotation curves of several well-measured galaxies.
Check that the resulting fits are comparable to dark matter halo models.
Verify that the same xi value used for Hubble tension also produces reasonable fits.
Assess whether the chi-field prediction is not ruled out by rotation curve data.

dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a dark matter alternative explanation for flat rotation curves using chi-field modified gravity, with a single parameter xi.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the ability to explain galaxy rotation curves without dark matter, consistent with existing cosmological tests.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: If removed, the chi-field framework loses a key observational consistency check, weakening its claim as a viable modified gravity theory.

Claiming superiority over dark matter models without full error analysis.
Interpreting consistency as proof of the theory.
kill_conditions: If rotation curve fits fail with xi constrained by Hubble tension.
If full error analysis shows significant discrepancy with observations.
If the chi-field model cannot reproduce flat rotation curves without fine-tuning.

plain_summary: This document describes a Colab notebook that tests whether the chi-field modified gravity can explain galaxy rotation curves without dark matter. It claims that using the same coupling constant xi that resolves the Hubble tension, the chi-field produces rotation curve fits comparable to dark matter models. However, it explicitly states this does not prove the chi-field is correct, only that it is consistent with observations. The notebook is reproducible but lacks full error analysis, so the claim is graded C and should be treated as a consistency test, not a proof.
